feeds.title: Bikepacking
feeds.description: Bikepacking.com is the leading resource for bikepacking routes, in-depth gear reviews, inspiration, planning insight, adventure stories, news, and events. Our mission is to inspire others to explore the far corners of the Earth by bicycle.

feeds.title: Sifter Goes (Bike) Riding
feeds.description: I live, work, ride, write and more in Wellington, New Zealand.

feeds.title: Chris Bennett's Bikepacking and Triathlon Blog
feeds.description: Read the blog to find race reports, training, gear and musings about triathlons, cycling and other exercises. This blog is by Chris Bennett, a 60+ year old who enjoys bikepacking, cycling, running and triathlons, even though he isn't particularly good at the latter (especially the swimming).

feeds.title: CyclingAbout.com
feeds.description: CyclingAbout is the most popular bike travel websites, creating resources for bicycle touring, bikepacking and other bike adventures. The website can assist you with technical resources, inspiration, reviews, videos, and more.

feeds.title: Bikabout Blog
feeds.description: Inspiring two wheeled tourism in cities across North America. Blog featuring posts about cities, scenic vistas, gear reviews, bicycle friendly businesses, family travel tips, transportation challenges and first class experiences.

feeds.title: Bikepacking Northern Nevada Blog
feeds.description: Bikepacking Northern Nevada showcases exploring Nevada backroads by bicycle as the forum for adventures. If off road touring, bikepacking, or wondering where this road leads interests you then maybe you will find some inspiration here. While this is not necessarily a 'how to' I will share my thoughts on gear choice, planning and preparation, and trip highlights.

feeds.title: Bikes or Death Blog
feeds.description: Bikes or Death is a podcast centered around the growing sport of bikepacking, adventure cycling, and the outdoors. The show features the amazing people who participate in these activities and contribute so greatly to the cycling community.

feeds.title: Dispersed Bikepacking Blog
feeds.description: Dispersed Bikepacking is a project by Katie and Andrew Strempke. Dispersed handmade bikepacking bags are designed to be used wherever your bike takes you. They've been tested on the Great Divide, Colorado Trail, and Arizona Trail, along with thousands of miles of backcountry chunk.

feeds.title: Farawayistan
feeds.description: Farawayistan is the place where a passion for bikepacking, gravel riding and photography comes together. Our mission is to show the world from the perspective of our handlebars and to tell unique stories about adventures.

feeds.title: Marley Blonsky Blog
feeds.description: I'm Marley Blonsky, a Seattle based bike-adventurer. Self-identifying as a fat woman, I believe that bikes can be a tool for community building, empowerment, education and fun. I'm an advocate for people of all sizes, genders, races, ages, income levels and abilities to be included and welcomed in the bike community. To that end, I am actively working with the bike industry, community groups and riders to create inclusive groups where all feel welcome to ride!

feeds.title: Taunus Bikepacking Blog
feeds.description: Self-supported bikepacking adventure. Taunus Bikepacking is a bike ride taking in all of the Taunus region. The fifth edition starts in Eppstein and uses unbeaten paths along well known and lesser known sights.

feeds.title: Pushbikegirl » Blog
feeds.description: I am Heike. Solo female traveling with a blue heeler around the world.

feeds.title: Bike Packers Magazine
feeds.description: If you enjoy going on fun adventures through bikepacking but have not found the right website to see all of the information on what bike-packing can offer - you are in for a treat at Bikepackers Magazine. Bikepacking has only become more popular over time as it's a low-cost way to do some traveling.

feeds.title: Justin Simoni » Bikepacking
feeds.description: Bikepacker, fastpacker, climber, and writer, based in Colorado. THE LONG RANGER is Justin Simoni - the character he performs as when pursuing his personal Trinity of Mountain Arts: trail running, mountain biking, and mountaineering.

feeds.title: Weekend Adventurers » Biking
feeds.description: If you're looking for places to ride, gear to use, or routes to follow, here are all of our posts about mountain biking, bikepacking, and gravel biking. Weekend Adventurers is a blog for anyone who loves to live their life adventurously. Packed full of guides, advice and reviews, this blog is here to inspire you to spend more time outdoors and to make the most of your spare time.

feeds.title: TomsBikeTrip.com
feeds.description: Hi I'm Tom Allen. I provide adventure cycle-touring inspiration and advice. I've travelled to over 40 countries on 4 continents on my bicycle. I'm here to help you get going on your next bike trip with planning & gear-buying advice, tips from the road, & more.

feeds.title: Highlux Photography Blog
feeds.description: The blog of Mark Watson & Highlux Photography. Here, you can find the full account of our Alaska to Patagonia, bikepacking journey, as well as more recent posts from New Zealand adventures both by bike and in the mountains.

feeds.title: Bikepacking Alliance Blog
feeds.description: Phil Snider is a bikepacking addict who also happens to be an above knee amputee. He creates technical resources, reviews, inspirational videos, how-to guides and more.

feeds.title: Cycling Around The World
feeds.description: I am Jin from South Korea. I have started cycling since 1st. Sept. 2011 without going back home through North America, Latin America, Africa, Europe, Middle East, Central Asia, South East Asia, and Oceania all by myself. When I was looking at Northern Lights in Canada 2010, I decided to cycle the world before traveling another planet. I didn't have any plan cause I had never had the experience of cycling trip overseas. Luckily I have found that I love adventure so much.

feeds.title: Bikepacking Roots News
feeds.description: Bikepacking Roots supports and advances bikepacking, the growth of a diverse bikepacking community, and access to and the conservation of the landscapes and public lands through which we ride.
